summary: Internal portal session claim desync preventing analytics dashboard login
description:
Issue summary: Multiple internal users intermittently receive 403 when loading the analytics dashboard (analytics-portal). Symptoms appear after recent Okta group membership changes; affected sessions are not picking up updated role claims until a hard re-auth.

Impact: ~12 engineers (observed) unable to access analytics dashboards or Jupyter notebooks for ~3-10 minutes during incidents; blocks troubleshooting and data exploration. No customer-facing impact but blocks internal ops during high-churn onboarding windows.

Environment: prod-us-east, internal VPC, analytics-portal behind sso-proxy (session cache + jwt-claim-middleware).

Steps to reproduce (intermittent):
1) In Okta admin, add user to a role-mapped group (e.g., data-analysts).
2) Trigger SCIM user-group update (via automated sync job or manual add).
3) Within 1-2 minutes, the user attempts to open analytics-portal while still having an active session cookie.
4) Portal returns 403 and shows "Insufficient role claims" in UI.
5) Clearing cookies or forcing SSO re-auth immediately restores access.

Observed logs and notes:
- sso-proxy logs show cached session token verified successfully but claim set does not include updated "redwood_roles" attribute.
- Identity webhook logs show SCIM user.update event delivered at 2026-03-10T15:18:43Z for user alice@redwood.com. sso-proxy logged session validation at 2026-03-10T15:18:45Z returning old claims.
- Okta system log entries indicate SCIM delivery latency spikes (~700ms) during churn windows.

Initial hypothesis: race between SCIM webhook delivery and session-claim-refresh path. When Okta updates group memberships, the SCIM hook correctly updates internal identity store, but the sso-proxy uses a session-bound cached claim snapshot and does not re-fetch claims until TTL expiry. If the SCIM update arrives before the session cache invalidation event, the portal continues to serve requests with stale claims leading to 403.

Temporary mitigation: Added a forced revalidate link in the portal UI (users can click to force a re-auth and refresh claims). Support instructed affected users to hard re-auth as a workaround.

Next steps: implement claim invalidation triggered by SCIM webhook (or push invalidation message to session cache). Also add metrics to correlate SCIM update times with session validation timestamps.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Add user to Okta group that is mapped to portal roles.
2) Immediately attempt to use analytics portal without logging out.
3) Note 403 with "Insufficient role claims".
4) Force re-auth -> access restored.
